Anthropic is upgrading Claude Sonnet, replacing Sonnet 5 with Sonnet 5.5 in June to become the best mid-sized model.

Claude Sonnet 5.5 elevates Anthropic's mid-sized models

Anthropic currently offers several AI models under Claude.

The three main models are Haiku (smallest, cheapest), Sonnet (mid-sized, mid-priced), and Opus (largest and most expensive of the three).

In addition, there is Fable/Mythos, which offers even greater capabilities and higher costs, representing Anthropic's top tier.

Today's new Claude model launch follows last week's debut of Opus 5.5. At that time, Anthropic promised to "in the coming weeks" upgrade Sonnet and Haiku.

Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 performs best on well-defined everyday tasks, such as fixing bugs, writing polished documents, presentations, and spreadsheets.

The company also highlights its design capabilities, from optimizing user interfaces to producing presentations with templates that require only minor adjustments before use.

Citing early testers, Anthropic describes Sonnet 5.5 as better suited to a collaborative role than Sonnet 5, with clearer writing and a speed appropriate for rapid iteration on simpler tasks.

Sonnet 5.5 maintains Sonnet 5's rates: $2 per million input tokens, $10 per million output tokens, and $0.20 per million cache reads.

Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 typically requires far fewer tokens than before to accomplish the same work, generating over 30% faster than Sonnet 5, making it the fastest Sonnet model ever.

Sonnet 5.5's cybersecurity capabilities match those of Opus 5, making it the first version to launch with the same cybersecurity protections and fallback mechanisms as Anthropic's top-tier models.

Its biosafety protections remain unchanged from Sonnet 5. Anthropic says both only target a small number of high-risk requests, leaving general software development and most life sciences work unaffected.
